question.worked_solution:
If we attempt to evaluate the limit by simply evaluating the function at $x=2$, we get an indeterminate form:

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}\frac{x-2}{2x-\sqrt{8x}} & =\frac{2-2}{2(2)-\sqrt{8(2)}}=\frac{0}{0}\end{aligned}
$$

So, we need to first simplify the limit. Since the radical is in the denominator, we can multiply the numerator and the denominator by the conjugate of the denominator. We get

$$
\begin{aligned}{lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}\frac{x-2}{2x-\sqrt{8x}} & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}\frac{(x-2)(2x+\sqrt{8x})}{(2x-\sqrt{8x})(2x+\sqrt{8x})} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}\frac{(x-2)(2x+\sqrt{8x})}{(2x)^{2}-{(\sqrt{8x})}^{2}} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}\frac{(x-2)(2x+\sqrt{8x})}{4{x}^{2}-8x} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}\frac{(x-2)(2x+\sqrt{8x})}{4x(x-2)} \\  & ={lim}_{x\to {2}^{-}}\frac{2x+\sqrt{8x}}{4x} \\  & =\frac{2(2)+\sqrt{8(2)}}{4(2)} \\  & =\frac{4+4}{8} \\  & =1.\end{aligned}
$$
